questions.stem: What is 「いけばな」?
questions.explanation: 「いけばな」 arranges flowers and branches by set principles. The tea ceremony is 「さどう」, calligraphy 「しょどう」 and paper folding 「おりがみ」.

questions.stem: What is 「しょどう」?
questions.explanation: 「しょどう」 is the way of writing, kanji and kana written with a brush and ink. Many schools teach it, and students write 「書きぞめ」, the first writing of the New Year, in January.

questions.stem: What is 「かぶき」?
options: A traditional theatre of large puppets
A slow masked drama with chanting
Comic storytelling by a single performer
Theatre with bold make-up and an all-male cast
questions.explanation: Kabuki actors, all men, play female roles too, and wear striking make-up called 「くまどり」. Puppet theatre is 「ぶんらく」, and the masked drama is 「のう」.

questions.stem: What is 「らくご」?
options: A poem of seventeen sounds about nature
Comic storytelling by one kneeling performer
A comic play performed by a large cast
A form of dance performed at summer festivals
questions.explanation: A rakugo performer kneels on a cushion and plays every character, using only a fan and a small cloth as props. The stories usually end with a punchline.

questions.stem: What is a 「はいく」?
options: A long poem telling a story
A short poem of 5, 7 and 5 sounds
questions.explanation: A haiku has three phrases of 5, 7 and 5 sounds and usually contains a word for the season, 「きご」. The longer 5-7-5-7-7 poem is the 「たんか」.

questions.stem: Matsuo Bashō, who lived in the 1600s, is best known for what?
questions.explanation: Bashō is the most famous haiku poet, and his frog poem 「ふるいけや」 is known across Japan. He also wrote travel journals that mix prose with haiku.

questions.stem: Which work is Katsushika Hokusai famous for?
questions.explanation: Hokusai's Great Wave is a woodblock print, 「うきよえ」, from his series of views of Mount Fuji. The Tale of Genji is a novel, Seven Samurai a film and Astro Boy a manga.

questions.stem: Who wrote The Tale of Genji, 「げんじものがたり」, about a thousand years ago?
options: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady at the imperial court
questions.explanation: Murasaki Shikibu wrote it in the early 1000s about life at the Heian court, and it is often called one of the world's first novels. The other three lived centuries later.

questions.stem: Tezuka Osamu, often called the 'god of manga', created which character?
questions.explanation: Tezuka created 「てつわんアトム」, Astro Boy, and shaped the style of modern manga and anime. Totoro comes from a film by Miyazaki Hayao.

questions.stem: Miyazaki Hayao is known for what?
options: Novels such as The Tale of Genji
Animated films such as Spirited Away
questions.explanation: Miyazaki co-founded Studio Ghibli and directed 「せんとちひろのかみかくし」, Spirited Away, which won the Academy Award for animated feature. The other works belong to Murasaki, Hokusai and Bashō.

questions.stem: Kurosawa Akira is famous as what?
questions.explanation: Kurosawa directed films such as Seven Samurai and Rashōmon, which influenced film-makers around the world. Rashōmon won the top prize at the Venice Film Festival.

questions.stem: Yukawa Hideki was the first Japanese person to win which award?
options: An Academy Award, for a film
questions.explanation: Yukawa won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1949 for predicting the meson, a particle linked to the force that holds the atomic nucleus together. The first Japanese literature prize came later, to Kawabata Yasunari.

questions.stem: What is 「お正月」?
options: The summer festival of the dead
questions.explanation: 「お正月」 is the New Year, the most important holiday of the year, when families gather. The summer festival for ancestors is 「おぼん」, and the star festival is 「七夕」.

questions.stem: What is 「はつもうで」?
options: The first day back at school
The first visit of the year to a shrine or temple
The first meal the family eats in the New Year
The first snow of the winter
questions.explanation: At 「はつもうで」 people pray for the year ahead, often in the first days of January. Many buy a fortune, 「おみくじ」, or a lucky charm, 「おまもり」.

questions.stem: What is 「おとしだま」?
options: Money given to children at New Year
Decorations put up at New Year
questions.explanation: Children receive 「おとしだま」, money in small envelopes, from relatives. New Year food is 「おせちりょうり」 and New Year cards are 「ねんがじょう」.

questions.stem: At 「せつぶん」 in February, what do people traditionally do?
options: Throw beans to drive out bad luck
Fly carp streamers outside the house
questions.explanation: People throw roasted beans, calling 「おにはそと、ふくはうち」, 'demons out, luck in'. Wishes on bamboo belong to 「七夕」 and carp streamers to Children's Day.

questions.stem: At 「七夕」, what do people traditionally do?
options: Throw roasted beans to drive out demons
Visit a shrine to pray for the year ahead
Give money in envelopes to young relatives
questions.explanation: 「七夕」 (たなばた), the star festival, falls on 7 July in most places. Wishes are written on strips called 「たんざく」. Note the special reading: neither kanji is read as usual.

questions.stem: On Children's Day, 「こどもの日」, 5 May, what do many families fly outside?
questions.explanation: 「こいのぼり」, carp-shaped streamers, fly for the children of the family. The carp swimming upstream stands for strength and success.

questions.stem: What is 「おぼん」?
options: A spring festival to view the cherry blossoms
An autumn festival to give thanks for rice
A winter holiday spent at a hot spring
A summer time to honour the spirits of ancestors
questions.explanation: During 「おぼん」, in summer, many people return to their family home, visit graves and join 「ぼんおどり」 dances. Viewing cherry blossoms is 「お花見」.

questions.stem: What do people do at 「お花見」?
questions.explanation: 「花見」, flower viewing, means cherry blossoms in spring, often with food and friends under the trees. Arranging flowers is 「いけばな」.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a 「神社」 and an 「お寺」?
options: A 神社 is in a city and an お寺 is in the mountains
A 神社 is for weddings and an お寺 is for festivals
A 神社 is Shinto and an お寺 is Buddhist
A 神社 is Buddhist and an お寺 is Shinto
questions.explanation: 「神社」 (じんじゃ) are Shinto shrines to the 「神」, gods or spirits, and 「お寺」 (おてら) are Buddhist temples. Many people visit both.

questions.stem: A 「とりい」 gate usually marks the entrance to what?
questions.explanation: The red or wooden 「とりい」 marks the way into a 「神社」. Temples have their own gates, called 「もん」, often with guardian statues.

questions.stem: Entering a Japanese home, what do you do in the 「げんかん」?
questions.explanation: The 「げんかん」 is the entrance hall, a step lower than the house. You take off your shoes there and often put on slippers.

questions.stem: Why do people say 「いただきます」 before a meal?
options: To ask for a second helping
To say the food tastes good
To give thanks for the food
questions.explanation: 「いただきます」, from the humble verb 'to receive', thanks everyone and everything that brought the meal. After eating, people say 「ごちそうさまでした」.

questions.stem: Why is it bad manners to stand chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice?
options: It tells the waiter you want the bill
It recalls an offering made at a funeral
It tells the cook you want more rice
It shows that you did not enjoy the meal
questions.explanation: Rice with chopsticks standing in it is offered to the dead, so it is avoided at the table. Passing food from one pair of chopsticks to another is avoided for the same reason.

questions.stem: What is 「おみやげ」?
options: A gift brought back from a trip
A gift given at a wedding
A gift sent at the end of the year
A gift given to a new neighbour
questions.explanation: People bring 「おみやげ」, often a local food, back from travel for family, friends or colleagues. Each region is known for its own.

questions.stem: In Japan, a deeper bow generally shows what?
options: That you disagree with the speaker
More respect or a more serious apology
That you are in a hurry to leave
That you know the other person well
questions.explanation: The deeper and longer the bow, the more respect or regret it shows. A quick nod suits friends and people you see every day.

questions.stem: In restaurants in Japan, what is the custom about tipping?
options: A tip of about ten per cent is expected
A tip is added at the till by law
Only the chef is tipped, not the staff
Tipping is not part of the custom
questions.explanation: Good service is treated as part of the price, so money left on the table may simply be returned to you.

questions.stem: How do you say 'ticket' in Japanese?
questions.explanation: 「きっぷ」 is a train or bus ticket. 「きって」 is a postage stamp, 「きっさ」 is short for 「きっさてん」, a café, and 「きっと」 means 'surely'.

questions.stem: On a train, the announcement says 「次は、京都です。」 What does it mean?
options: This train is going to Kyoto.
We have now arrived in Kyoto.
questions.explanation: 「次」 (つぎ) is 'next', so this tells you the coming station. Arriving now would be 「京都に着きました」, and a train's destination is announced as 「京都行き」.

questions.stem: What is a 「おうふくきっぷ」?
questions.explanation: 「おうふく」 is there and back. A one-way ticket is 「かたみち」, and a reserved seat is 「していせき」.

questions.stem: On the shinkansen, what is a 「じゆうせき」?
questions.explanation: 「じゆう」 is 'free' in the sense of freedom, so you may sit anywhere in those cars; you still pay. Free of charge is 「むりょう」, and a reserved seat is 「していせき」.

questions.stem: What does 「二つ目のかどを右にまがってください。」 mean?
options: Turn right at the second traffic lights.
Turn right at the second corner.
Turn left at the second corner.
questions.explanation: 「二つ目」 is 'the second', 「かど」 a corner, and 「右にまがる」 to turn right. Traffic lights are 「しんごう」, and going straight is 「まっすぐ行く」.

questions.stem: Read: 「駅を出て、まっすぐ行くと、左にゆうびんきょくがあります。」 Where is the post office?
options: On the right if you go straight from the station
Inside the station, on the left
On the left, before you leave the station
On the left if you go straight from the station
questions.explanation: 「駅を出て」 is 'leave the station', 「まっすぐ行くと」 'if you go straight', and 「左に…があります」 'there is … on the left'. Plain form + 「と」 gives a natural result.

questions.stem: What is a 「りょかん」?
options: A business hotel near a station
questions.explanation: A 「りょかん」 usually has tatami rooms, futons and dinner served in a set style, often near a hot spring, 「おんせん」.

questions.stem: What does 「一泊二日」 mean on a booking?
questions.explanation: 「一泊」 (いっぱく) is one night's stay, from 「泊まる」, and 「二日」 (ふつか) is two days. A stay of two nights would be 「二泊三日」.

questions.stem: What does 「よやくしたいんですが。」 mean?
options: I'd like to make a booking.
I'd like to cancel my booking.
I'd like to change rooms, please.
I'd like to check out now.
questions.explanation: 「よやく」 is a reservation, and 「〜たいんですが」 is a polite, open-ended way to make a request. Cancelling is 「キャンセル」.

questions.stem: In a shop, what does 「もう少し安いのはありますか。」 mean?
options: Do you have a slightly cheaper one?
Can you make this one a bit cheaper?
Is this one the cheapest you have?
Do you have a slightly bigger one?
questions.explanation: 「もう少し安い」 is 'a little cheaper' and 「の」 stands for 'one', so you are asking for another item. Asking for a discount on this item would be 「安くしてもらえますか」.

questions.stem: At a restaurant, the staff ask 「何名さまですか。」 What do they want to know?
options: What you would like to order
How many are in your group
questions.explanation: 「名」 here is the counter for people, read 「めい」, with 「さま」 for politeness. 「名前」 is a name, which is why the question is easy to misread.

questions.stem: What do shop staff mean when they say 「いらっしゃいませ」?
questions.explanation: 「いらっしゃいませ」 greets customers as they come in. Customers don't reply with the same words; a nod is enough. Thanks at the end is 「ありがとうございました」.

questions.stem: What is 「おせちりょうり」?
options: Special food eaten at New Year
A lunch box taken to school
questions.explanation: 「おせちりょうり」 are New Year dishes packed in layered boxes, each with a meaning, such as long life or good harvests. A lunch box is 「おべんとう」.
